checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: theorem9_listUpdate_progress and theorem9_measure_listUpdate_progress prove exact group replacement and the claimed total-loss decrease.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: theorem10_update_count_le_loss_div and theorem10_measure_update_count prove both the initial-loss and unit-loss bounds.
checked_proof_steps.scope: Finite-support and arbitrary measurable population laws.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: theorem20_costSensitive_minimizer_is_certificate_maximizer and its measure analogue prove the exact reduction.
checked_proof_steps.scope: Binary labels, ternary predictors, and arbitrary measurable population laws.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Expected induced ternary cost is the negative of the derived pair's certificate objective, so a cost minimizer is a certificate-objective maximizer.

defects.acceptance_condition: Prove the exact finite-support statement, give a checked atomless counterexample to the literal arbitrary-law statement, prove the arbitrary-label modelwise almost-everywhere replacement, and recover the common-null-set actionwise form for countable labels.
defects.repair_obligation: Replace the pointwise arbitrary-law equivalence by an almost-everywhere equivalence, or restrict to an atomic setting in which every support point has positive mass.
defects.resolution_evidence: observation4_bayesOptimal_iff_groupwiseOptimal proves the finite-support statement; observation4_arbitraryDistribution_pointwise_iff_counterexample gives the atomless witness; observation4_kernelAEModelwiseOptimal_iff_groupwiseOptimal proves the arbitrary-label modelwise almost-everywhere equivalence; observation4_kernelAEBayesOptimal_iff_groupwiseOptimal proves the common-null-set actionwise form for countable labels.
defects.source_claim: Bayes optimality, defined through pointwise conditional risk on the support, is equivalent to optimality against every alternative model on every subgroup.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The correction changes only null-set representatives. The arbitrary-label modelwise theorem preserves every distributional loss and group-integral conclusion, the countable-label bridge recovers actionwise Bayes optimality, and the literal pointwise statement is correctly rejected.

defects.acceptance_condition: Prove an explicit failure-probability tail for the exact sparse transcript family, then derive the complete FalsifyAndUpdate and monotone-process guarantees from the same checker event.
defects.repair_obligation: Eliminate the undefined confidence symbol delta-prime and replace the invalid transcript-count inequality by an exact count that supports the same adaptive accept/reject semantics.
defects.resolution_evidence: theorem11_adaptive_certificateCheckerRun and its measure analogue use the exact family U*(U+1)^floor(2/epsilon) and prove the tail 2*N*exp(-n*epsilon^2/32); Theorems 12 and 14 propagate that event through their complete state machines.
defects.source_claim: The adaptive certificate checker and its downstream update processes satisfy the stated accept/reject guarantees at the displayed logarithmic sample size.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The accept/reject guarantees and logarithmic dependence on the submission horizon are preserved; only the undefined symbol and defective finite counting step are replaced by an exact bound.

defects.acceptance_condition: Define one transcript-driven process and prove completion, checker soundness, accepted-update bounds, and the advertised groupwise monotonicity conclusion.
defects.repair_obligation: Give the external and repair proposals one shared adaptive checker state and restart the protected-history scan after every accepted repair so that no newly introduced regression is skipped.
defects.resolution_evidence: monotoneBountyStateFromTranscript, monotoneBountyStepFromDecision, restartMonotoneRepairScan, and theorem14_monotoneBounty formalize and verify the shared-state restarting process.
defects.source_claim: MonotoneFalsifyAndUpdate feeds external proposals and repair proposals through CertificateChecker and recursively repairs losses on protected historical groups.
defects.status_impact_rationale: This makes the intended recursive repair semantics precise and proves the advertised monotonicity result without changing its population guarantee.

defects.acceptance_condition: Retain the literal non-strict guard, prove that every queried prefix fits the floor(2/epsilon) sparse code, and prove that the complete output contains at most one additional acceptance.
defects.repair_obligation: Distinguish the acceptance count in queried transcript prefixes from the count in the final transcript after the last issued query.
defects.resolution_evidence: numberAccepted_le_checkerAcceptanceBudget supplies the queried-prefix bound used by checkerRunAuxGuaranteed_of_sparseFamilyAccuracy. certificateCheckerRun_numberAccepted_le_budget_add_one proves the exact final-transcript bound for the literal source runner.
defects.source_claim: The printed non-strict guard processes a proposal while NumberAccepted is at most 2/epsilon, while the proof says the transcript contains at most 2/epsilon acceptances.
defects.status_impact_rationale: No adaptive query is generated from the possible final extra acceptance, so the exact sparse-family confidence theorem and every accept/reject guarantee remain valid.

defects.acceptance_condition: Prove the per-round transition on D_t and the full high-probability theorem with a rounded horizon, exact optimization-call bound, and exact total sample count.
defects.repair_obligation: Use the fresh round block D_t in both the optimization and stopping test, and give the nonintegral quantity 2/epsilon an integer-safe loop interpretation.
defects.resolution_evidence: trainByOptStep uses its TrainingRound sample, trainByOptRoundBudget is ceil(2/epsilon), and theorem16_trainByOpt_sourceRounded plus measureTheorem16_trainByOpt_sourceRounded prove the full guarantee and resource bounds.
defects.source_claim: TrainByOpt partitions the sample into T=2/epsilon blocks and optimizes and tests one certificate at every round before either halting or applying ListUpdate.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The source proof already requires independent round blocks. The repair is a pseudocode subscript and rounding correction with unchanged asymptotic sample and oracle complexity.

defects.acceptance_condition: Prove the stated uniform deviation with the same group in the population and empirical terms and preserve the source VC dependence.
defects.repair_obligation: Replace the undefined empirical group symbol g_p by the quantified group g.
defects.resolution_evidence: lemma15_vc_uniform_convergence and measureLemma15_vc_uniform_convergence prove the corrected same-group objective bound with an explicit VC radius.
defects.source_claim: Uniform convergence bounds the difference between the population and empirical certificate objectives for every quantified g in G and h in H.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The source quantifiers and proof make g the only intended group; g_p is an undefined typographical substitution and the corrected theorem has the advertised content.

defects.acceptance_condition: Prove that disagreement loss equals a constant minus the certificate objective and deduce the same ERM argmin-to-objective-argmax conclusion.
defects.repair_obligation: Replace the proof's use of disagreement-normalized proportions as population masses by an identity with a group-independent offset.
defects.resolution_evidence: disagreementLoss_eq_constant_sub_binaryCertificateObjective and its measure analogue establish the exact identity; lemma22_disagreementERM_maximizes_fixed_model and measureLemma22_disagreementERM_maximizes_fixed_model derive the printed lemma unchanged.
defects.source_claim: An empirical-risk minimizer on the disagreement-labelled sample maximizes the fixed-model certificate objective over the group class.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The theorem statement, assumptions, and optimizer are unchanged; only the printed normalization argument is replaced.

defects.acceptance_condition: Prove two-sided epsilon local optimality, the 2/epsilon strict-update bound, the exact ceil(2/epsilon) best-response-round bound, a counterexample to arbitrary-start positivity, and recovery of a genuine positive certificate from positive initialization.
defects.repair_obligation: Test the two coordinate gaps separately so stopping certifies both final-coordinate inequalities, add exactly the premise needed to ensure the returned locally optimal pair has positive certificate value, and include the terminal stopping test in the integer oracle-call accounting.
defects.resolution_evidence: coordinateAscentStep and measureCoordinateAscentStep implement two-gap updates; theorem23_coordinate_update_bound and its measure analogue prove the strict-update rate; measureCoordinateAscentFuel_rounds proves the exact ceil(2/epsilon) loop-round and per-class oracle-call envelope; theorem23_local_optimum_without_positive_certificate is the one-point counterexample; theorem23_coordinateAscentLoop_positive_certificate and measureTheorem23_coordinateAscent_sourceRounded_positive_certificate prove the positive-initialization repair.
defects.source_claim: From an arbitrary initial pair, alternating ERM returns after at most 2/epsilon ERM calls over each class with a positive certificate that is epsilon-locally optimal in both coordinates.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The same alternating-ERM method retains the local-optimality, O(1/epsilon) convergence, oracle, and model-class guarantees. The pseudocode tests the two final-coordinate gaps separately, and only the positive-certificate clause needs an explicit positive-start premise.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The arbitrary-population interfaces for Definitions 1--7, Observation 4, Theorems 8--16, and the optimization reductions through Theorem 23.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Population expectations are taken under an arbitrary probability measure; losses, models, groups, adaptive submissions, and bad events carry the measurability or integrability premises needed for those expectations and probabilities to exist.
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: These premises do not impose finite support, parametric classes, or densities; they expose the standard definedness conditions implicit in the source notation.
model_conventions.why_needed: The paper writes expectations and conditional/group losses without spelling out their measure-theoretic definedness conditions.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Definitions 2 and 5 and all certificate objectives, in both finite-PMF and arbitrary-measure developments.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The mass-weighted group-loss numerator is the total primitive; conditional group loss is totalized to zero at mass zero, and every divided source display is recovered on positive-mass groups.
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: No theorem depends on the chosen zero value; source divided formulas are claimed only under positive group mass.
model_conventions.why_needed: Conditional loss on a null group is undefined in ordinary probability notation, while the paper permits arbitrary subgroups.
